topIssues.author: joshklop
topIssues.body:
The elasticity multiplier is already guaranteed to be greater than zero:

https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/5401e3a46d4e193bbe5400b9c3948d8098c8692d/packages/contracts-bedrock/src/L1/SystemConfig.sol#L449

but we can add that check to the derivation pipeline for redundancy in case we accidentally remove it from the contract. cc @mds1

topIssues.title: op-supernode: Interop Implementation
topIssues.author: axelKingsley
topIssues.body:
# Context
Supernode is a sandbox/container framework for OP Nodes to extend their protocol. The primary use-case for this paradigm is interop.

Supernode is built to support behaviors beyond individual op-node instances, so lots of the scaffolding is already built out!

# Sub-items

## Interop Application Behaviors
Make the application interact with the chain in all the ways required to do interop, besides evaluating interop.
- check that chains are ready
- record results to a database
- record metadata about progression

## Interop Algo
Literally do Interop
- Pull Logs into LogDB
- Validate all Logs
- Expose invalid blocks

topPRs.title: feat: Add support for Interop Migration using OPCM v2
topPRs.author: 0xiamflux
topPRs.body:
## Add Interop Migration Support for OPCM v2

Implements Interop Migration functionality to work with OP Contracts Manager v2.

### Changes
- **Version Detection**: Use semantic version comparison (`version() >= 7.0.0`) instead of feature flags
- **Input Structure**: Restructure `MigrateInputV1` with nested `GameParameters` and `Proposal` structs
- **Type Updates**: Change `DisputeGameConfig.GameArgs` from `Hash` to `bytes` for correct ABI encoding
- **CLI Separation**: Split `migrate` and `migrate-v2` into separate commands

### Testing
- Add tests for interop migration v1 and v2
- Add migration input encoding tests
- Add invalid game type validation tests

topPRs.title: feat: Add `add-game-type-opcm-v2` command to op-deployer
topPRs.author: 0xiamflux
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Adds the `add-game-type-opcm-v2` command to the `op-deployer` acting as a wrapper around the Upgrade command. This command allows users to add new game types to chains using the OPContractsManager V2.

## Changes

- **New CLI Command**: Added `add-game-type-opcm-v2` command in `op-deployer/pkg/deployer/manage/flags.go`

  - Wraps the existing upgrade command with the default embedded upgrader

- **Command Handler**: Implemented `AddGameTypeOPCMV2CLI` function in `op-deployer/pkg/deployer/manage/add_game_type.go`

  - Delegates to `upgrade.UpgradeCLI(embedded.DefaultUpgrader)` for actual execution

- **CLI Flags**: Added supporting flags for the new command:
  - `--config`: Path to the config file containing upgrade input
  - `--override-artifacts-url`: Optional override for artifacts URL
  - `--outfile`: Path to write output (defaults to stdout)

### Testing

  - Tests for missing required flags (`--config`, `--l1-rpc-url`)
  - Tests for invalid config file paths and malformed JSON
  - Tests for missing required fields in config

topPRs.title: fix(sysgo): allow OS to assign ports for opreth, rbuilder, rollup-boost
topPRs.author: bitwiseguy
topPRs.body:
# Overview
Follow-up to https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/18684 to reduce likelihood of port collisions within sysgo.

Updates `op_rbuilder`, `opreth` and `rollup-boost`: by default pass port 0 for all ports to let the OS assign a port number. Since there is not currently a rpc command to retrieve the port numbers after they're assigned, parse the logs to extract the port numbers

# Remaining Work
While this pr reduces the likelihood of port collision issues, the following changes would have to be made to the corresponding rust codebases before we can completely eliminate the use of `getAvailableLocalPort` within sysgo.

  1. rollup-boost RPC port - needs to log "RPC server listening on {addr}" after binding
  2. kona metrics port - tracked in https://github.com/op-rs/kona/issues/2987

topPRs.title: op-node: validate EIP-1559 params in derivation pipeline
topPRs.author: devin-ai-integration
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Adds redundant validation for EIP-1559 parameters (denominator and elasticity) in the derivation pipeline when processing `SystemConfigUpdateEIP1559Params` events. This provides defense-in-depth against the contract-level checks being accidentally removed.

The SystemConfig contract already enforces `denominator >= 1 && elasticity >= 1` at [L449](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/5401e3a46d4e193bbe5400b9c3948d8098c8692d/packages/contracts-bedrock/src/L1/SystemConfig.sol#L449), but this adds the same validation in the client-side derivation code.

**Validation logic:**
- Rejects params where denominator is 0 but elasticity is non-zero
- Rejects params where elasticity is 0 but denominator is non-zero  
- Allows (0,0) which is a valid special case that gets translated to pre-Holocene protocol constants downstream

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] Verify that `eip1559.DecodeHolocene1559Params` correctly decodes the 8-byte params from `params[24:32]` - the encoding is `uint256(_denominator) << 32 | uint64(_elasticity)` where denominator is first 4 bytes and elasticity is last 4 bytes
- [ ] Confirm the (0,0) case is intentionally valid - this matches behavior in `engine_consolidate.go` where 0,0 gets translated to pre-Holocene constants
- [ ] Run `go test -short ./op-node/rollup/derive/... -run TestProcessSystemConfigUpdateLogEvent -v` to verify tests pass

### Notes

Closes #18625

Link to Devin run: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/2349b811f31f4b039ac7cd25ae5db8ae
Requested by: Kelvin Fichter (@smartcontracts)
